title: Self-Admitted Technical Debt in LLM Software: An Empirical Comparison with ML and Non-ML Software
role: targeted counterevidence to an overbroad no-longitudinal-evidence claim; not a member of the frozen sample
evidence_note: 477 repos, 159 per group, and millions of comment events; uses survival analysis. Reports 44% of 377 manually sampled comments as false-positive/undefined/unknown; calls out age confounding between post-2022 LLM repos and older ML projects. SATD is only an explicit-comment proxy.
relevance: Shows longitudinal repository-history work exists while its proxy, false-positive, selection, and age limits leave causal AI effects unresolved.

title: Evolving with AI: A Longitudinal Analysis of Developer Logs
role: targeted counterevidence and construct-boundary check; not a member of the frozen sample
evidence_note: Analyzes 800 JetBrains IDE devices (400 regular JetBrains AI Assistant users, 400 non-users), plus 62 survey responses and five interviews. Typed characters proxy productivity and debugging events proxy code quality. Authors explicitly say the goal is not causal effect attribution; the exposure definition misses use of other AI products in non-user classification.
relevance: Establishes multi-year workflow measurement, but not semantic correctness or causality.

title: Debt Behind the AI Boom: A Large-Scale Empirical Study of AI-Generated Code in the Wild
role: targeted counterevidence and provenance/measurement boundary check; not a member of the frozen sample
evidence_note: Reports 304,362 explicitly AI-attributed commits in 6,275 public repositories and tracks static-analysis issues. It lacks a clean human-only baseline, includes only public repositories with explicit Git attribution and Python/JavaScript/TypeScript, and excludes architectural/documentation debt; authors note attribution and issue matching remain imperfect.
relevance: Shows large-scale issue-lifecycle tracking exists without resolving counterfactual human comparison or semantic outcomes.

title: Are ‘Solved Issues’ in SWE-bench Really Solved Correctly? An Empirical Study
role: targeted counterevidence against claiming reference-patch/test-oracle limitations are novel; not a member of the frozen sample
evidence_note: Across three issue-solving tools on SWE-bench Verified, reports 7.8% of plausible patches counted correct while failing developer tests; 29.6% behaviorally diverge from reference patches, and manual review deems 28.6% of divergent patches certainly incorrect. Divergence alone is not proof a patch is wrong.
relevance: Patch/reference-oracle validity is already studied. The remaining batch72 idea is to apply multi-oracle validation in the selected SATD-repair setting, pending a wider novelty search.
